title: The Unwritten Bridge
premise: In the river city of Vellmark, on the eve of a revolution nobody has named yet, Hazel Yarrow cuts type in her father's print shop while the government's census takers quietly catalog who owns what — and who can be taken. When census taker Elias Brand asks Hazel one question too many about a hidden press, he is ordered to report her family; instead he falsifies the record, and the two are bound together in finishing the shop's final commission: ten thousand pamphlets that must be printed and carried across the frozen river before the ice breaks. As soldiers close in and her father's memory begins to fail him, Hazel must choose between preserving the shop that defines her and destroying it to save the people inside it. The book ends with the bridge of ice cracking at dawn: the pamphlets cross, the shop burns behind them, and Hazel, carrying only her father's smallest cutting knife, walks into the revolution she helped set in type.
about_author: A. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about the people whose hands made history legible.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On a gray morning in Vellmark, Hazel sorts type by touch while her father, losing his memory in slow increments, mistakes her for his late wife. She measures their life in what could be carried if they had to run. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath ordinary labor.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Census taker Elias Brand arrives to count hearths and hands, but lingers over the back room where a second press sits under canvas. He asks about its owner; Hazel lies well enough to worry herself. Emotional beat: the first crack between obedience and curiosity.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered by his superior, Magistrate Corven, to inventory the Yarrow shop for seizure, Elias instead brings them a commission: ten thousand pamphlets, printed fast, paid in coin that smells of conspiracy. He tells himself it's penance. Emotional beat: complicity disguised as kindness.

chapters.title: What the Father Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hazel's father briefly surfaces from his confusion and recognizes the pamphlet text as sedition he helped draft thirty years ago — then forgets again by supper. Hazel realizes the revolution has been waiting in her family all along. Emotional beat: grief braided with inheritance.

chapters.title: Ice Roads
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias scouts the frozen river and maps the crossing while Corven grows suspicious of the census discrepancies. A soldier friend warns him that falsified records end in the same cell as printers. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into commitment.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Reasons
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The print run begins; the shop becomes a furnace of ink and secrecy as neighbors take shifts and Hazel teaches Elias to set type by lamplight. Between shifts, an unspoken tenderness takes shape neither will name. Emotional beat: love growing in the margins like marginalia.

chapters.title: Corven's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Corven confronts Elias with the altered records and offers him a bargain: deliver the Yarrows and keep his name clean. Elias signs a false confession instead, buying three days. Emotional beat: the point of no return, crossed deliberately.

chapters.title: The Breaking Day
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Soldiers reach the far bank early; the last two thousand pamphlets are still wet. Hazel makes the choice her father cannot: burn the shop's ledgers and presses rather than let them be seized, keeping only the type they can carry. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Across
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the blue dark before dawn, the convoy crosses the groaning ice — Hazel, Elias, her father, and neighbors hauling sledge-loads of pamphlets as the river begins to shift beneath them. Her father, lucid for one clear moment, walks beside her. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Bridge
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. On the far shore they watch the ice fail and the shop's chimney fold into smoke; the pamphlets pass hand to hand through the crowd like a lit fuse. Hazel keeps her father's cutting knife and begins setting new type in exile. Emotional beat: mourning and beginning in the same breath.
